results.note: Sermo de decem virginibus: Searched extensively; no English translation found. Medieval sermon text on the Parable of the Ten Virgins exists in Latin but appears untranslated.
Notitia historica: No English translation found in searches of medieval translation databases, CCEL, or scholarly sources.

Vita S. Ambrosii Autperti: Biographical work about 8th-century Benedictine monk. Search results focused on Ambrose of Milan biography by Paulinus rather than Autpert's vita. No English translation identified.
Circuli decemnovenales: A calendrical/computational text on nineteen-year cycles. No English translation found despite searches.

Vita Bedae (first version): Anonymous hagiography of Bede. Medieval Manuscripts catalog references Chris Grocock and Ian Wood preparing Oxford Medieval Texts edition, but full translation availability unclear from searches.

Vita Bedae (second version, different recension): Same work as 3422 but different manuscript location. Oxford Medieval Texts edition by Grocock & Wood may cover this, but specific translation details unconfirmed.
Chronicon antiquissimum: Medieval chronicle from 8th century. No English translation found in searches of translation databases or medieval sources bibliographies.
Chronicon breve: No English translation identified. Searched medieval chronicle translations; not located.
Computatio: Brief computational text (58 words). No English translation found; likely too fragmentary to warrant independent translation.
Chronologia Bedae: Brief chronological text (421 words). No English translation identified despite searches for Bede-related computistical works.
Problemata: Brief text (436 words). No English translation found. Very short problemata collections typically untranslated.
Chronicon episcoporum Metensium: Chronicle of the Bishops of Metz. No English translation found in searches of medieval chronicle databases.
Commonitorium: Anonymous ecclesiastical text in PL 96 (not Vincent of Lérins's Commonitorium). No English translation identified.
De apparitione S. Michaelis: modern English translations exist per Johnson (2005) and Everett (2016) treatments of the Monte Gargano apparition narrative.

Expositio missae Romanae: Liturgical exposition of the Roman Mass. Searched for 8th-9th century versions; no English translation found (Bonaventure's 13th-century Expositio exists in translation but is different work).
Gesta Dagoberti: Anonymous early-9th-century biography of King Dagobert I. Described as 'extremely unreliable' historically but no English translation identified in searches.

Gesta regum Francorum: Distinguished from Gesta Francorum et aliorum Hierosolimitanorum (First Crusade chronicle, which has translations). The 'regum Francorum' version has no identified English translation.
Inscriptio codicis: Brief inscription/colophon (281 words). Too fragmentary to warrant standalone translation; no English version identified.
Tractatus: Generic title (2,218 words). Insufficient distinctive information to identify specific work; no translation found.
Annales veteres: Medieval annals. Searched medieval annals translation databases; this specific 'Annales veteres' not identified with an English translation.
Carmen: Anonymous medieval poem (2,965 words). Generic title makes identification difficult; no English translation identified.
Genealogia Caroli Magni: Genealogical text on Charlemagne (297 words). Likely historical/genealogical compilation; no English translation found.
Liber genuinus censuum: Ecclesiastical census/rental register (5,555 words). Administrative text; no English translation identified.
Provinciale vetus: Appears to be provincial/administrative listing (2,714 words). No English translation found.
Versus: Anonymous medieval verses (1,074 words). Likely poetry; generic title; no translation identified.
Excerptum ex litaniis rhythmicis: Fragment of rhythmic litanies (107 words). Too brief and specialized; no English translation identified.

Poenitentiale Theodori cum aliis capitulis collatum: Included in McNeill, John T. and Gamer, Helena M., Medieval Handbooks of Penance: A Translation of the Principal Libri Poenitentiales and Selections from Related Documents (Columbia University Press, 1938; 1990 reprint).
Poenitentiale Theodori cum testimoniis collatum: Variant version of Theodore's Penitential; covered in McNeill & Gamer Medieval Handbooks of Penance (1938/1990).

Vita Alcuini: First complete Latin edition with French translation by Christiane Veyrard-Cosme (Brepols, 2017) identified, but no comprehensive English translation located. Limited English translations of some of Alcuin's other works exist.
Regula secunda: Anonymous monastic rule (656 words). No English translation identified in searches of monastic rule translations.
Regula tertia: Anonymous monastic rule (655 words). Third in a series of rules; no English translation found.

Annales Laurissenses et Eginhardi: Known as Royal Frankish Annals (Annales Laurissenses maiores). English translations: Scholz, Bernhard Walter and Rogers, Barbara, Carolingian Chronicles: Royal Frankish Annals and Nithard's Histories (University of Michigan Press, 1970); also King, Paul David, Charlemagne: Translated Sources (1987).

Vita Ludovici: Anonymous vita of Louis the Pious. Disambiguation needed between this and Thegan's Gesta Hludowici imperatoris (836-7); Colgrave & Mynors and Astronomer versions found but attribution/translation status for this specific anonymous version unclear.
Appendix ad Vitam S. Eigilis: Appendix to the life of Saint Aigilis/Eigil. No English translation found despite searches for this saint's vita and appendices.

Liber poenitentialis: Anonymous 8th-9th century penitential. Likely included in McNeill & Gamer Medieval Handbooks of Penance if it matches their source materials, but not explicitly confirmed in searches.
Vita S. Aldrici: Anonymous 9th-century vita of Aldric of Le Mans (d. 856), composed shortly after his death at Le Mans. No English translation identified in searches.

Vita S. Ansegisi: Likely confusion with Vita Ansgarii (biography of missionary Anskar by Rimbert). Robinson, Charles H., Anskar, The Apostle of the North, 801-865 (SPCK, London, 1921) is a pd-ingested English translation, but Ansegis was an abbot, not the missionary Anskar. Work identity ambiguous.

Appendix ad Pontificale Agnelli: Also known as Liber Pontificalis Ecclesiae Ravennatis by Andreas Agnellus. English translation: Deliyannis, Deborah Mauskopf, trans., The Book of Pontiffs of the Church of Ravenna (Catholic University Press, 2004).
Gesta Aldrici: Anonymous account of Aldrici, Bishop of Le Mans (d. 856). Similar subject to Vita S. Aldrici but different genre/form. No English translation identified.
Carmen de conflictu veris et hiemis: Medieval debate poem (Spring vs. Winter; 331 words). Likely allegorical verse; no English translation found.
Epitaphium Pippini et Drogonis: Epitaph in verse for Pippin and Drogio (69 words). Very brief; no English translation identified.
Sermo de translatione S. Amandi: Sermon on the translation/relocation of relics of Saint Amand (1,322 words). No English translation found in searches.
De Miraculis S. Barnardi: Miracles of Saint Bernard (488 words). Brief hagiographical account; no English translation identified.
De festivitatibus apostolorum: Liturgical/hagiographical account of apostolic feasts (6,638 words). No English translation found despite searches for apostolic feast material.
De translatione S. Barnardi: Narrative of the translation/relocation of Saint Bernard's relics (236 words). No English translation identified.
